WANDR is a Perplexity wide-research benchmark of 500 tasks requiring search for tens to hundreds of entities with cited facts in structured records; the metric is soft F1 (precision of verified content vs recall of the requested collection), with entity rows failing format validation dropped rather than failing the task.
quote: The primary metric is “soft F1,” which balances precision (how much of the model’s solution is verified) against recall (how much of the requested fact collection it completed).

claim: Anthropic ran a modified WANDR: offline web search and fetch against a frozen index (Perplexity uses the live web), Claude Opus 4.6 as judge (Perplexity uses GPT-5.4), slightly different prompts; results are not directly comparable to reported competitor numbers.
quote: Because the tools and grading logic differed from Perplexity’s harness, our results are not directly comparable to reported numbers on competitor models.

claim: WANDR Claude runs used web search, web fetch, programmatic tool calling, code execution, and a 980k-token task budget; the grader re-fetches cited URLs and a judge model decides whether the references support the solution.
